codeReview.summary: Implementation covers core happy paths, but two blocking parity regressions remain: binary-match output ignores -c/-l semantics in binary-enabled mode, and max-count diagnostics are computed from reportable lines (affected by -v) instead of baseline match-count behavior.

issues.description: Binary files are handled before mode-specific output logic, so --search-binary/-u with -c or -l prints 'Binary file X matches.' instead of ag-parity count/filename output (reproduced on tests/edge-cases/binary-files with --search-binary -c and --search-binary -l).

max_count_hit uses count_total_matches() based on reportable lines and invert-match branching, which diverges from ag diagnostics for -v (e.g., --max-count=3 -v NEEDLE few-matches.txt emits ERR in ag but not in rust-ag).

sharedStateObservations.observation: rewrite-worker procedure does not explicitly remind workers to update scenario grouping/manifests when introducing new parity matrix groups.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: handoff.skillFeedback.suggestedChanges includes: 'The rewrite-worker skill could mention updating manifest hashes when adding scenario groups to scenarios.json'; commit also updates manifests/scenarios.json with core-edge-cases tags.

summary: Reviewed transcript skeleton and commit diff for rust-core-binary-symlink-largefile-maxcount. Found two blocking parity gaps in binary-enabled mode handling and max-count diagnostics under invert-match, so this feature review fails pending fixes.
